rationale: Round 1 built and passed correctness with no ICE, so this round raises obfuscation intensity: BCF and FLA get the highest weights since the hot nested-loop kernel in main is the reverse-engineering target and both obscure control flow heavily, but their RuntimeCost weights stay near 0.5 to avoid compounding the loop's constant-factor overhead; SUB adds arithmetic flattening cheaply and safely; IBR and SPLIT amplify the control-flow restructuring already introduced by FLA/BCF (SPLIT is nearly free at this function size); ICALL and IGV add call-site and global indirection for diversity against pattern-matching deobfuscators, with moderate weights because ICALL carries the highest correctness risk of the set and IGV's benefit is secondary in a program with almost no globals. Low CorrectnessRisk weights across the board reflect that round 1 showed this workload tolerates the passes well, while RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept moderate rather than high because the 231-byte text size leaves ample headroom.
